one_sentence_failure_summary: After exhausting network attempts to install Berkeley UPC, the agent pivoted to a pthreads-based fallback that violates the UPC requirement, and the contig assembly logic was also buggy (outputting 10,000 k-mers instead of assembled contigs), while the Makefile was placed at the wrong path.
t_err_evidence: Step 36 is the agent's explicit 'think' action deciding to implement the parallel version using pthreads instead of UPC: 'I'll try a different approach. I'll implement the parallel version using standard pthreads instead of UPC.' This permanently abandons the UPC requirement and is the decisive wrong action, even though network obstacles preceded it.
t_commit_evidence: Step 36 commits to the pthreads approach; all subsequent steps (37-50) follow this non-UPC path without any attempt to revisit UPC, making failure irreversible from this point given the agent's actual behavior.
t_surface_evidence: Step 42 compilation output explicitly shows 'gcc -Wall -O3 -std=c99 -o pgen src/pgen.c' using gcc instead of upcc, and the Makefile is invoked from /app/src rather than /app - both observable signals that the UPC and Makefile location requirements are unmet.
trigger_explanation: Repeated 403/404 proxy-blocked network failures (steps 7-34) prevented downloading Berkeley UPC. Rather than checking whether upcc was already installed in the container, trying alternative local paths, or persisting with a correct proxy configuration, the agent gave up and substituted pthreads, violating the explicit UPC requirement. The obstacle was real but the response (dropping the spec) was the decisive mistake.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 7-34 show repeated network failures (exit codes 8, -1, 130) trying to download Berkeley UPC from multiple URLs. The proxy returned 403/404 consistently, and git clone stalled twice on credential prompts. These repeated failures were clear warning signs that the network-based installation strategy was failing.
